    // The bundled lib's receiver-bearing interfaces declare `self` as their first
    // parameter, so the colon form and the explicit-self dot form -- the two ways
    // Lua reaches the same metatable function -- both check.
    
    local text: string = "hello world";
    
    local upper: string = text:upper();
    local piece: string = text:sub(1, 5);
    local repeated: string = text:rep(2);
    local length: number = text:len();
    local reversed: string = text:reverse();
    local lowered: string = text:lower();
    local code, nextCode = text:byte(1, 2);
    local codeType: number | nil = code;
    
    local explicitPiece: string = text.sub(text, 1, 5);
    local explicitUpper: string = text.upper(text);
    
    // The namespace form is unchanged: it names the receiver as an ordinary
    // argument.
    local nsPiece: string = string.sub(text, 1, 5);
    
    // Arity and argument types are now measured against the receiver's slot, so a
    // colon call reports the WRITTEN argument that is wrong.
    text:sub("one");
             ~~~~~
